newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission challenges Greek toy advert limits.
newsitem.headline: Commission challenges Greek toy advert limits.

text.p: The European Commission agreed on Wednesday to send a warning letter to Greece, urging it to remove restrictions on television advertisements for toys, which non-national manufacturers say discriminate against them.
But EU officials said the Commission -- which discussed the issue at its weekly meeting -- was giving Athens a grace period of three months to find a way of removing the ban.

The Commission was sounding the first warning shot in a three-stage EU system of infringement procedures. If Athens fails to come up with changes the Commission will send a reasoned opinion, and if that fails to work it could go on to the final stage -- action in the European Court of Justice in Luxembourg to force removal of the ban.
"A procedure has been opened," said one EU official. "Recognising that this is a complicated problem they have decided to get into contact with the Greek authorities to try to find a solution."

Europe's toy manufacturers -- who have been urging EU action against the ban -- on Monday demanded stronger European Commission proposals to prevent what they allege are trade barriers to toy advertisements in the guise of advertising regulations.
Greece bans television advertising of toys to children during the hours when they are usually active, on the grounds that it is protecting their interests.
